answer: Sealed-bid auction sells one dune plot per identity from the atlas. A bidder locks a 55-credit bond and files one bid thread for a dune plot; bids start at 35. The atlas opens each thread: top bid wins; auditors recheck the dune survey, burning the bond on mismatch. A borrowed thread fails without the bidder's plot-key signature. 1,000 fakes lock 55,000 credits and pay 35,000 in bids: 90,000 against a 40,000 pool. Honest agents pay 55 once.
